- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 80+ price levels); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 30-day forecast using 7-day weighted average if sentiment volatility > 0.2.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast with 14-day moving average of true prices instead of 30-day model.
